title: Planning on Graphs: Dijkstra's Algorithm and A*

contract.reader: An engineer or student who has read entry 1, knows what a graph and a queue are and reads Python
contract.problem: Planning on a discretized configuration space and knowing which search to use, what it guarantees and what it costs
contract.outcome: Build a grid or visibility graph; run and prove Dijkstra's algorithm; choose an admissible and consistent heuristic; predict the effect of weights, any-angle search and incremental replanning; see why grids do not scale with dimension
contract.contribution: One 15 by 26 map on which every search is run and counted, short proofs of optimality and of the weighted bound, and a measured arm grid on the torus
contract.evidence: Proofs in the text, programs with real output, Dijkstra 1959, Hart et al. 1968, Pohl 1970, Koenig and Likhachev 2002, Nash et al. 2007, Harabor and Grastien 2011 and others (numbers recomputed in the 2026-10-24 live review)
contract.limitations: Uniform-cost grids in the measurements; D* Lite described without its bookkeeping; counts depend on tie-breaking
